solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Criticise Dame blocking demands for way to identify comedian? (3,3,5)

indicators.note: the pair stands in the way inside CALLS, splitting it

blocks.note: to pan a show is to criticise it
DBE, Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire
calls = demands; PAN DBE goes inside after CA

annotation.surface: A critic sets about a pantomime dame who is getting in the way of a comic's needs.
annotation.walkthrough: The title Dame is abbreviated DBE, the honour that confers it. The cap and bells was the court jester's headgear, so it marked out the comedian of the court.
annotation.definitionFit: The belled cap was the jester's badge of office, the thing that identified the court comedian.

entries.clue: Efficient secretary blocking message (7)

indicators.note: PA sits inside CABLE, stopping it up

blocks.note: PA = personal assistant; goes inside CA…BLE

annotation.surface: A capable secretary intercepts a message.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Efficient secretary' reads as one phrase, but 'Efficient' is the definition and the secretary is only PA.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who gets the job done well is both.

entries.clue: Furious policeman receiving nothing in support — one’s a source of repeated documents (11)

definitions.text: one’s a source of repeated documents

indicators.note: HOT COP takes O in between its parts
the whole lot sits inside PIER

blocks.note: a pier supports a bridge; it wraps round the rest after its P

annotation.surface: An angry officer ends up with nothing in the way of backing.
annotation.walkthrough: Two insertions stack: O goes into HOT COP, then HOTOCOP goes into PIER as P…IER.
annotation.definitionFit: A photocopier turns out copy after copy of a document.

entries.clue: Prompt, say, with plague on the rise (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading bottom to top

blocks.note: to dun is to pester someone for payment

annotation.surface: A cue given while a pestilence spreads.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prompt, say' looks like a definition with its example marker, but 'say' is EG in the wordplay. The whole EGDUN rises to read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: a gentle push with the elbow prompts someone to act.

entries.clue: Delivery documentation variously bathetic and terrific (5,11)

indicators.note: the letters are set out in various different orders

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 16 letters; 'and' just joins the two words

annotation.surface: A review calls some paperwork on a delivery both anticlimactic and wonderful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' sounds like parcels and couriers; here it is the delivery of a baby.
annotation.definitionFit: A birth certificate is the official record of a baby's delivery.

entries.clue: Sprang around most of field, like many rabbits? (3-5)

indicators.note: LOPED goes round the field
AREA loses its last letter

blocks.note: loped = bounded along; it wraps round the field after LOPE

annotation.surface: Something leapt about a meadow, as rabbits do.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a rabbit bounding round a field, and the answer is a rabbit's feature.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: lops are rabbit breeds whose ears hang down.

entries.clue: Be prepared for a row or this phase goes awry (4,3,4)

indicators.note: the phrase goes wrong, its letters out of order

annotation.surface: A warning to brace for a quarrel in case this stage of things goes badly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A row' reads as a quarrel; it is rowing a boat.
annotation.definitionFit: To ship the oars is to set them in the rowlocks, ready to row.

entries.clue: Divide part that’s got dry on the inside (6)

indicators.note: the dry word sits inside BIT

blocks.note: a bit = a part; it holds SEC between BI and T

annotation.surface: Split off a piece that has dried out inside.
annotation.walkthrough: SEC is the wine-list word for dry.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: the answer means to cut in two equal halves, a precise kind of dividing.

entries.clue: Secured maximum value from statistics? (5)

blocks.note: the mathematician's term for the upper limit a quantity can reach

annotation.surface: Someone has squeezed the most out of the figures.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one idea, but it splits after 'Secured'. The second half is the mathematician's upper bound.
annotation.definitionFit: Something bound is secured; an upper bound is the maximum a quantity can take.

entries.clue: Frivolous, dissipated, welcoming British drizzle (14)

indicators.note: SCATTERED takes the others in

annotation.surface: A dissolute, giddy person likes British drizzle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dissipated' looks like a second description of a rake; it only means scattered.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a flighty, unfocused mind takes nothing seriously.

entries.clue: Careful to limit river breach, albeit minor (6)

indicators.note: CANNY bounds R on both sides

blocks.note: canny = shrewd, cautious; R goes after C

annotation.surface: A cautious engineer keeps a river's small breach under control.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is flood defence; the 'breach' is only a small crack.
annotation.definitionFit: A cranny is a small crack or opening, a breach on a tiny scale.

entries.clue: Abandon some surgery led by doctor (4)

indicators.note: whatever leads goes at the front, so the doctor comes first

annotation.surface: A surgeon walks away from part of an operation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some surgery' is not a hidden-word signal here; it just means one operation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you give up a plan, a subject or a friend.

entries.clue: Indecently humorous as BA airline flounders (11)

indicators.note: the letters struggle and fall out of order

annotation.surface: A comedian makes crude jokes as British Airways struggles.
annotation.walkthrough: BA is British Airways; here it is just two letters for the mix. Rabelais was the bawdy French comic writer.
annotation.definitionFit: Rabelaisian humour is coarse and earthy, after Rabelais's bawdy satires.

entries.clue: Literary genre initially lacking in motion, mostly calm (7)

indicators.note: SCI-FI loses its first letter
'in' puts one piece inside another, so CIFI goes within PAC
PACE loses its last letter

blocks.note: PACE, a rate of motion, cut short; wraps as PA…C

annotation.surface: A literary genre that barely moves is almost soothing.
annotation.walkthrough: The ocean's name comes from the same root: the Pacific was named for its calm.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym from Latin pax, peace: a still, untroubled sea or temperament.

entries.clue: Not at the front, a runner’s last to secure prize? On the contrary (8)

indicators.note: one part is held inside the other
the prize holds A R, not the other way round

blocks.note: a reward = a prize; opens after RE

annotation.surface: A trailing runner hopes to win a prize.
annotation.walkthrough: Read literally, A R would take in the prize; 'On the contrary' flips it so REWARD takes in AR.
annotation.definitionFit: Rearward means towards or at the back, not at the front.

entries.clue: German article on learner in school, not the brightest one? (7)

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so DER comes after
a learner in school is enrolled inside it, so L sits within POD

blocks.note: a school of whales is a pod; L goes after P

annotation.surface: A German-speaking pupil at school is a bit slow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'School' is the one for whales and dolphins, not pupils.
annotation.definitionFit: A plodder works slowly and steadily, not the brightest of the class.

entries.clue: Flowering plant Paul replanted around border (7)

indicators.note: PAUL's letters are set out anew
the new order goes round RIM

annotation.surface: A gardener named Paul moves a flower round the edge of a bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Border' pulls towards the flower bed; it is just RIM.
annotation.definitionFit: The primula is the primrose family of flowering plants.

entries.clue: Bitter passion involving Bishop recalled in account (7)

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up in, so IRE wraps round B
IBRE is called back, running the other way
the result sits inside ACC

blocks.note: ire = anger; B goes after I
acc. = account; ERBI goes after AC

annotation.surface: An angry dispute over a bishop is written up in a report.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passion' suggests love; here it is the angry sort.
annotation.definitionFit: Acerbic means sharp and bitter in tone.

entries.clue: Impoverished adherent unfortunately inconsolable (6-7)

indicators.note: the word comes out badly, letters jumbled

annotation.surface: A penniless follower is past all comfort.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram slices across the hyphen: BROKE plus N gives BROKEN.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone broken-hearted is overwhelmed by grief and cannot be consoled.

entries.clue: Perceived welcoming old woman back as an imposition on staff (5,4)

indicators.note: a host welcomes a guest inside, so FELT takes CRONE in
the whole is read backwards

blocks.note: a crone is an old woman

annotation.surface: Someone sensed an old woman returning as a burden on the employees.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'staff' is the musical stave, not employees, and a clef is placed on it at the start of each line.
annotation.definitionFit: A tenor clef is a symbol set on a musical staff to fix the pitch of its lines.

entries.clue: That man about to get taken aback for a time (5)

indicators.note: 'about' as in round about: HE goes round COP
the whole is read backwards

blocks.note: he = that man; opens after H
to cop is to get or catch

annotation.surface: A man is startled for a moment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' reads as surprised; it is a reversal signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym on a grand scale: a whole era or age of history.

entries.clue: Damage unknown following on agreement (7)

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so the unknown goes after ON

blocks.note: x, y and z are unknowns in algebra

annotation.surface: An agreement comes after harm has been done.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a link word; it is part of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: people in accord live together without discord.

entries.clue: He or I perhaps will lead a railway — that’s obvious (10)

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so the element comes first

blocks.note: He is helium and I is iodine, both chemical elements

annotation.surface: Either he or I will run a railway, and that's plain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'He or I' look like pronouns; they are the chemical symbols for helium and iodine.
annotation.definitionFit: An echo of Sherlock Holmes's 'Elementary, my dear Watson', said of something plain to see.

entries.clue: Dance round after smack (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, what comes after sits lower, so the round goes below the smack

blocks.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
a go = a round, a turn

annotation.surface: A dance in which a slap is followed by another turn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Round' wants to be O; here it is GO, a turn.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Argentine ballroom dance.

entries.clue: Crazy mother backing murderer (6)

indicators.note: to back is to move backwards, so the murderer is read in reverse

blocks.note: CAIN, the first murderer in Genesis, reversed

annotation.surface: A mad mother supports a killer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as supporting; it reverses the murderer.
annotation.definitionFit: Maniac can be used as an adjective meaning wildly crazy.

entries.clue: Check opening article with list and come up with nothing new (8,3,5)

blocks.note: a ship heels when it lists to one side

annotation.surface: An editor checks the first article and the list and finds nothing fresh.
annotation.walkthrough: 'List' is a ship's lean, HEEL, not a list of items; 'with' is W, not a link.
annotation.definitionFit: To reinvent the wheel is to waste effort producing something that already exists.

entries.clue: Head of monastery, settlement not given initial precedence (8)

indicators.note: CITY loses its first letter

annotation.surface: A prior's town is denied the right to go first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initial precedence' reads as one phrase, but 'initial' belongs to the deletion.
annotation.definitionFit: Priority is precedence, the right to come first.

entries.clue: A bowman piercing old man in part of leg (7)

indicators.note: A TELL goes into PA like an arrow

annotation.surface: An archer's arrow hits an old man in the leg.
annotation.walkthrough: The bowman is William Tell, who shot an apple off his son's head.
annotation.definitionFit: The anatomical name for the kneecap, the bone at the front of the knee joint.

entries.clue: “PROHIBITIONIST CHAP WITH COMMERCIAL POLICY”? (6,8)

annotation.surface: A newspaper front page shouts about a man who wants to ban things.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is printed in capitals and quotes, so it looks like a banner headline itself; that is the definition, while the words also give the parts. 'With' only joins.
annotation.definitionFit: A banner headline is a large-type headline across the page, as the clue is styled.

entries.clue: European moving into region without a cost (7)

indicators.note: E comes in to take a place
'without' means lacking, so the region loses its A

blocks.note: an expanse is a wide region
the A of EXPANSE is taken out
E = European, and it fills the gap

annotation.surface: A European relocates to a region with no charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without a cost' reads as free; 'a' belongs to the wordplay and 'cost' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: money laid out on something, as in 'at great cost'.

entries.clue: Prominent figure with concern about end of luncheon after cold dish (6,3,5)

indicators.note: 'about' as in surrounding: CARE goes round the N
the other pieces follow CHILL

blocks.note: an icon is a celebrated figure

annotation.surface: A celebrity worries about the end of lunch, served after a cold course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cold dish' looks like one phrase for a salad; 'cold' is CHILL, and 'dish' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Chilli con carne is a spicy meat and bean dish.

entries.clue: Depressing experience? Try another way (4-3)

blocks.note: something that puts you off or dampens your spirits
a side road leading away from the main one

annotation.surface: After a disheartening setback, someone suggests a different approach.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition is the road sense: a turn-off is another way to go.
annotation.definitionFit: A turn-off dampens enthusiasm; a turn-off is also a road leading away.

entries.clue: One chronicling chap’s century, suppressing regressive attitude (9)

indicators.note: TON holds RIA down inside it
to regress is to go backwards, so AIR is read in reverse

blocks.note: a ton = a hundred; opens after TO
an air = a manner, attitude; reversed to RIA

annotation.surface: A man writes about his century, keeping backward views quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a writer of the times; the century is TON, a hundred.
annotation.definitionFit: A historian is one who chronicles past events.

entries.clue: Very good joke recalled: something worth displaying? (3-2)

indicators.note: PUN is called back, reading the other way

blocks.note: a pun is a joke, reversed

annotation.surface: A cracking joke brought back seems worth putting on show.
annotation.walkthrough: PI for pious is a crossword standard.
annotation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a picture pinned on the wall to be displayed.

entries.clue: Strasbourg’s ready with external, dubious rationale (7)

indicators.note: 'with' means together with, so EXT is attached to PRET

blocks.note: prêt = ready in French, the language of Strasbourg

annotation.surface: Strasbourg has a readymade, questionable excuse.
annotation.walkthrough: Strasbourg signals French, so 'ready' becomes PRÊT.
annotation.definitionFit: A pretext is a false reason given to hide the real one.

entries.clue: Clumsy person near to where MPs vote (5)

blocks.note: lob, an old word for a lout or bumpkin

annotation.surface: An oaf is close to the voting place.
annotation.walkthrough: MPs vote by walking through the division lobbies of the House of Commons.
annotation.definitionFit: In Parliament, MPs record their votes by passing through the Aye or No lobby.

entries.clue: Quantity of chocolate surely transformed with a good piece of confectionery (6,5)

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

blocks.note: A as it stands, joins the fodder

annotation.surface: A chocolate bar is surely turned into a nice sweet.
annotation.walkthrough: SURELY, A and G together make LEYSUGAR; barley sugar is a British boiled sweet.
annotation.definitionFit: Barley sugar is a hard amber-coloured boiled sweet.

entries.clue: Bachelor, one in post with English sweetheart (9)

indicators.note: 'in' puts B I within the post
'with' means along with, so E is tacked on

blocks.note: a column is a post or pillar; opens after COLUM

annotation.surface: A single man in a job has an English girlfriend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Post' reads as a job; it is a pillar. Columbine is Harlequin's sweetheart in the old pantomime.
annotation.definitionFit: Columbine is Harlequin's beloved in commedia dell'arte and pantomime.

entries.clue: Small amount left in accommodation (5)

annotation.surface: A little is left over in the lodging.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a roadside hotel for motorists is one kind of lodging.

entries.clue: Barrier to communication worried court in Iran (4,7)

indicators.note: the letters are worried into a new shape

annotation.surface: An Iranian court is anxious about a communications blackout.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder's political flavour suits the answer, the Cold War divide.
annotation.definitionFit: The Iron Curtain was the Cold War barrier cutting off contact between East and West.

entries.clue: American writer’s sense of smell repulsed, taking in sea at Calais (7)

indicators.note: NOSE is pushed back, reading the other way
to take in a lodger is to house them, so ESON houses MER

blocks.note: a nose for things; reversed to ESON, opens after E

annotation.surface: An American author holds his nose at the sea at Calais.
annotation.walkthrough: Calais signals French, so the sea is MER. Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American essayist.
annotation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a nineteenth-century American essayist and poet.

entries.clue: Greek food spread on a knockout type of bread (11)

blocks.note: a span is a spread, a stretch

annotation.surface: A Greek spread served on a stunning kind of bread.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a food spread in this surface; it is SPAN. 'On' only joins.
annotation.definitionFit: Spanakopita is a Greek spinach and feta pie in filo pastry.

entries.clue: Broadcast left disharmony, dismissing writer’s latest lightweight stories (7,7)

indicators.note: the writer's R is sent out of FRICTION

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship

annotation.surface: A broadcast caused friction by dropping an author's new light stories.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' is PORT, the nautical left side.
annotation.definitionFit: Airport fiction is light paperback reading sold to travellers.

entries.clue: Filmed willing American entering borders of Canada (2,6)

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the American goes between Canada's borders

blocks.note: first and last letters of Canada; opens after C

annotation.surface: A keen American crosses into Canada while being filmed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Willing' is ON, as in 'you're on'.
annotation.definitionFit: The phrase means in front of a running film or TV camera, so being recorded.

entries.clue: Government: source of some anger on the golf-course? (8)

indicators.note: a source is where a thing starts, so take the first letter of some
in an across clue, anger on the tee comes after it

blocks.note: the tee is where each golf hole starts

annotation.surface: Government is the cause of some fury on the links.
annotation.walkthrough: Steerage here is the old sense of steering or direction, not the cheap deck of a ship.
annotation.definitionFit: Steerage means steering, guidance, hence government of a state.

entries.clue: Stake reputation ultimately on no Scottish radio equipment (8)

indicators.note: the last letter of reputation
in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the pieces run in order

blocks.note: an ante is a poker stake

annotation.surface: A Scot refuses to bet their reputation on a radio.
annotation.walkthrough: NAE is Scots for 'no'.
annotation.definitionFit: Antennae are aerials for sending or receiving radio signals.

entries.clue: Redirection of fishing gear starts to catch hundreds — smelt, is it? (6)

indicators.note: sending something in the opposite direction reverses it, so NETS runs backwards
the first letters of catch hundreds

blocks.note: first letters of catch and hundreds

annotation.surface: A trawler's nets swing round and haul in hundreds of smelt.
annotation.walkthrough: Smelt is a fish, which fits the fishing surface; here it is the past tense of smell.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a foul odour is something smelt, and the question mark flags the verb.

entries.clue: A bit sozzled to start with, partway through drink (7)

indicators.note: only the first letter of sozzled

annotation.surface: Someone gets a little drunk halfway through a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A bit sozzled' reads as tipsy; 'A bit' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym for a tiny amount, as in 'just a little'.

entries.clue: Unexpected fish, a lone catch at sea (10)

indicators.note: the letters are all at sea, confused

annotation.surface: An angler out at sea lands a single surprising fish.
annotation.walkthrough: The coelacanth was thought extinct for millions of years until one was caught in 1938, hence 'unexpected'.
annotation.definitionFit: The coelacanth is a fish known only from fossils until a live one was caught in 1938.

entries.clue: Content of quite a challenging lecture (5)

indicators.note: the answer is what the phrase contains

annotation.surface: The content of a lecture is rather hard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lecture' looks like a noun after 'challenging'; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym as verbs: to give lectures is to instruct students.

entries.clue: Maestro’s laughter interrupted by start of tense silence (7)

indicators.note: HOOT is broken into by the other letters
the first letter of tense

blocks.note: a hoot = a burst of laughter; opens after HO

annotation.surface: A conductor's laughter is cut off by a tense hush.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's after Maestro stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A hotshot is a brilliant, skilled person, a maestro.

entries.clue: Wagner opera: nothing to a Frenchman and almost nothing to an American (6)

indicators.note: ZIP loses its last letter

blocks.note: ZIP, US slang for nothing, cut short

annotation.surface: A Wagner opera means nothing to the French and not much to Americans.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a cultural jibe; both 'nothings' are just foreign words for zero.
annotation.definitionFit: Rienzi is Wagner's early opera about a Roman tribune.

entries.clue: One not going out after retirement (9)

definitions.text: One not going out after retirement

blocks.note: surface: someone who stays at home; meant: someone who does not drop off to sleep
surface: after leaving work; meant: after going to bed

annotation.surface: A pensioner who stays at home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' reads as leaving work, and 'going out' as socialising; they mean going to bed and dropping off.
annotation.definitionFit: An insomniac cannot get to sleep after retiring to bed.

entries.clue: Crows: “Bequests published! You can’t escape the truth!” (6,4,3)

blocks.note: a murder is the collective noun for crows
a book that is out is published

annotation.surface: Someone gloats that the wills have been made public at last.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crows' reads as a verb, gloating; it is the birds, whose group name is a murder.
annotation.definitionFit: The proverb 'murder will out' means the truth always comes out in the end.

entries.clue: I will follow Manchester United football team initially in civilian gear (5)

indicators.note: a follower comes behind, so I goes at the end
first letters of football team

blocks.note: first letters of football and team

annotation.surface: A fan will follow Manchester United, turning up in plain clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: Mufti is the military word for civilian clothes worn off duty.
annotation.definitionFit: Mufti is plain clothes worn by someone who usually wears a uniform.

entries.clue: Sense dull person’s in charge (5)

blocks.note: a log is a dull, inert person; 's = is

annotation.surface: Common sense says the boring one is the boss.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's of 'person's' is 'is', joining LOG to IC.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym as in 'there's no sense in that': sound reasoning.

entries.clue: Slightly crazy orbit, perhaps incomplete? Mine wasn’t (7)

definitions.note: the definition is the astronaut speaking: his orbit was not incomplete

indicators.note: RING loses its last letter

blocks.note: a ring is an orbit, perhaps, cut to RIN

annotation.surface: A dotty orbit that didn't come full circle; someone insists theirs did.
annotation.walkthrough: The last words are Yuri Gagarin's voice: in 1961 the first man in space made one complete orbit, so his was not incomplete.
annotation.definitionFit: Gagarin's flight completed a full orbit of the Earth, so his was not incomplete.

entries.clue: Official weather forecast possibly a burden (7)

blocks.note: a ref = a referee, a match official

annotation.surface: An official forecast of the weather may be a nuisance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Burden' is the old musical sense: the chorus of a song, not a load.
annotation.definitionFit: A burden is a song's recurring chorus, a refrain.

entries.clue: Rugby people may be mostly moving single set of rugby posts? (7)

indicators.note: SINGLE's letters shift about

annotation.surface: Rugby fans are mostly shifting one set of goalposts.
annotation.walkthrough: The first 'Rugby' is the town in Warwickshire, England, that gave the game its name; the second is the sport.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional fact: the town of Rugby lies in the English Midlands, so most of its residents are of that nationality.

entries.clue: Techie recalled study involving basic element of education? (4)

indicators.note: the whole is called back, read the other way
to involve is to wrap up in, so the study wraps round R

blocks.note: a den is a private study; opens after D
one of the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic

annotation.surface: A techie remembers a study built round the basics of learning.
annotation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic, so R stands for a basic of education.
annotation.definitionFit: A nerd is an obsessive technical type, a techie.

entries.clue: Line I understand, provided by one modern composer (6)

annotation.surface: A modern composer's single line is one I can follow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Provided by' just joins the wordplay to the composer. György Ligeti was a Hungarian avant-garde composer.
annotation.definitionFit: György Ligeti was a twentieth-century Hungarian composer.

entries.clue: Require large European vessel to show embroidery (11)

annotation.surface: A big European ship is needed to exhibit some stitching.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' is a boat, CRAFT, which fits the sewing answer by a second sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A broader term: any craft done with a needle, of which embroidery is the chief example.
